title: What the end state can do
text:
Absorb any arbitrary content — text, code, music, a legal filing, a scraped record, any modality — and read it, not summarize it, into one lossless, addressable structure: the EOT/GFP cube, the same taxonomy regardless of what went in. Every referent in that structure is a monad, "for someone," carrying its own universe rather than being a bare string; one address refers losslessly to the whole thing it names.

At any point in that structure — any cursor, any referent, any moment — answer "what is this, here, given these priors, given this other selected content" by returning the fold: the addressed, provenance-carrying state of everything relevant at that point, with atmosphere (the ground already stood in), lens (what's being aimed at), paradigm (the frame willing to be revised), and significance (how much this matters, measured against a real null, never asserted) attached.

Generate, when the ask calls for producing something new, by rendering the fold rather than asking a model to invent past it: restructure at the GFP/SVO level (parse to structure, address it, edit only what's actually revisable, reassemble), never rewrite freely. The model is the mouth — it renders what the structure has already, mechanically, licensed; it never supplies content the structure hasn't earned.

Run two tiers by design, not by accident: a fast, cheap, always-on System 1 (a small parser, a perceptron, whatever is fast enough to run on everything) that gets most of it right through sheer statistical concentration of ordinary usage, and a slow, deliberate, context-relative System 2 (ablation-grain-pressure's shape: embed with and without the token in question, measure the delta, weigh it against real provenance-tagged distributions, return a parliament of votes and a revisable pressure, never a verdict) invoked exactly where System 1 admits it doesn't know — never where a model is simply asked to guess.

Do real work in the world with this: civic and legal accountability (Eviction Overwatch, CaseLink, MNPD network audit, ALPR abuse detection) where the grounding discipline (Mozi: it is in the bytes the eyes and ears can witness, or it isn't) is the actual product, not a decoration on top of a language model.

Keep every organ separately owned and named (the Handle system, the archon-holocracy registry) so no one session or one person has to hold the whole thing in their head, and so "who fixes this" is always answerable by checking a real registry, not by guessing or by defaulting to whoever's in the room.
basis: Synthesized from this session's own work and the project's standing memory (referent-model-not-pointers, holonic-objects-in-slots, fold-instant-cursor-vision, fold-s1-s2-parallel-models and its second instance in the parser, modality-transfer, restructure-not-rewrite, the atmosphere-lens-paradigm essay, the archon-holocracy registry) — recorded, not invented, on the user's own direction: 'create a vision of the end state.'

title: What the end state explicitly cannot do — and should never claim to
text:
Never claim an objective, final category for any token, referent, or claim. Every settled tag is a high-confidence default on a continuum, not a different epistemic class from a typed gap — "shed" and "dog" are the same mechanism at different points on the same distribution, not a hard case and an easy case. A system that forgets this and starts asserting fixed kinds has stopped being this project and become the thing it was built to refuse.

Never close the ladder. This project's own repeatedly-rediscovered shape (the wheel that doesn't close, the ring that recurs at rising altitude, the MHC order-13 true negative, the atmosphere-lens-paradigm essay's own thesis) says a final, complete, "done" version of this system would be exactly the false objectivity everything else here refuses. There is no version of this vision that reaches "finished, no further revision needed" — that outcome is excluded by the same logic that makes the rest of it honest.

Never fix a real ceiling with more of the same lever. Measured this session: gold-based retraining transferred on 1 of 4 newly-targeted patterns even when built carefully to generalize — supervised fixing has a real, now-quantified ceiling, not just a theoretical one. And a whole construction class (reported-speech with an interrupted, coordinated subject) has no projective UD analysis at all — the parser architecture cannot represent the correct answer regardless of training data. When a ceiling like that is found, the honest move is to name it and change the approach, not spend another round of the same fix hoping for a different result.

Never let a model act as a groundless oracle. Not Claude, not a bigger local model, not "ask it and see" — a model may render what a mechanical structure has already licensed, or it may propose a bridge that gets mechanically verified before being kept, but it may never be the thing a judgment rests on with nothing checking it. This is the line this whole session kept finding on the wrong side of: a fabricated UD citation, an invented speech act, an adversarial verifier confidently rejecting a rule that turned out to be correct once actually checked against real documentation. The rule exists because the failure mode is real and was caught happening, more than once, in this exact session.

Never build in a vacuum. No new archon gets spawned, no ownership gets declared absent, without checking both naming systems (the Handle table and archon-holocracy/archons.json) first — lesson #75, paid for by getting it wrong once already. Work on any piece of this vision routes through whichever archon already owns that piece, or names the gap honestly if none does, rather than one session freelancing across all of it.

Never claim 100% on anything measured against real, open-ended material. Not parser accuracy, not summary fidelity, not pocket-discovery precision. The right number to report is always the honestly measured one, including when it's a partial win, a null result, or a discovered ceiling — never a rounded-up claim of completeness.
basis: Same synthesis basis as vision-can; the two are deliberately written as a pair (what it does / what it will never claim to do) per the user's own framing.

title: How this vision gets chased, not just stated
text:

Anyone — any session, any archon, any scheduled routine — reads the current fold of THIS document the same way any other document in this pipeline gets read, and appends a revision when something changes, rather than editing a fixed spec in place.

Ownership, checked against the real registries before any new work starts (per lesson #75): Chomsky (native/kernel/universal-grammar.js, eot-rich.js, english-parser.js, clause-tense.js) owns the parser/syntax substrate this session pushed on directly. No current archon owns ablation-grain-pressure.js's live wiring or the cursor-addressable fold interface itself — both are named gaps, not silently assigned, until an archon is actually spawned for them following the Handle-table-plus-registry check.

The concrete next actionable steps, in the order this session's own findings license them, not in order of ambition: (1) unblock the shared Ollama /api/embed contention so build-ablation-grain-prior.mjs can complete a real run — infrastructure, not code. (2) Run eval/the-fold/ablation-pressure-calibration.mjs for real once centroids exist, and only wire ablationPressureFor live if that calibration actually licenses per-case trust, per the standing rule already in the code. (3) Replace this session's ad hoc agglomerative pocket-discovery with a properly-powered, established method (the gap statistic or a real mixture-model comparison) before trusting pocket counts on real data — the synthetic tests this session ran found the ad hoc version underpowered, honestly, not fixed. (4) Only after 1-3: begin the actual cursor-addressable fold interface — the piece that has been described three times this session and built zero times.

Henry, narrative) 58 claims from 140 points, 3 unresolved; war-and-peace-ch45.md (Tolstoy, translated 19th-century prose) 14 claims from 44 points, 1 unresolved. Re-tested Ollama at the top of this cycle: still down, steps 1-2 remain blocked.

Re-tested Ollama at the top of this cycle: still down, steps 1-2 remain blocked. REVISION, 2026-09-26 (scheduled cron firing, pursuing obs:15's own named question): before writing more foldAt code, tried to find a REAL, already-motivated use for its siblings/ancestors in a generation-shaping stage, rather than inventing one. Read three candidate files' actual logic (not just names or comments): hunt.js's huntGround (already found, two cycles ago, to be a false-friend "ground" concept -- evidentiary source material, unrelated); finish.js's takesUp (checks whether a part's opening sentence "takes up" a being or word from the previous part's closing sentence -- works entirely through referent resolution and word overlap on raw text, never touches a GFP claim); loop-check.js's measurePiece/judgeLoop (measures whether a loop preserved anchors and answered the task's questions -- works through anchorsFor/carries on the piece's own text, never a GFP claim either). None of the three has an unmet need that foldAt's holon-addressed claim context would fill; each already solves its own adjacency/coherence problem through a different, working, non-claim-based mechanism. Wiring foldAt into any of them now would be manufacturing a use for it, not fulfilling one already there -- exactly the invented-purpose mistake this session's own standing rule (measure, don't assume) exists to catch.

This is not a dead end for foldAt, but it does redirect the real next step: either (a) foldAt's value is as a genuinely NEW capability (an interactive query/inspection surface over already-generated material, not a silent improvement folded into logic that already works its own way), which has never been attempted and would need its own honest scoping, not a forced retrofit; or (b) a deliberately DESIGNED experiment -- pick one specific generation decision, build a foldAt-informed alternative, and measure it against the current approach on real material -- which is a real, bounded project of its own, not something to back into by searching existing files for an accidental fit. Which of these two paths is worth pursuing is an open decision this revision names but does not make.

Anyone — any session, any archon, any scheduled routine — reads the current fold of THIS document the same way any other document in this pipeline gets read, and appends a revision when something changes, rather than editing a fixed spec in place.

Ownership, checked against the real registries before any new work starts (per lesson #75): Chomsky (native/kernel/universal-grammar.js, eot-rich.js, english-parser.js, clause-tense.js) owns the parser/syntax substrate this session pushed on directly. LaVar (LAVAR.md, eval/lavar/) owns grading the reader against real material and keeping the mistake corpus this project's own honesty depends on. Grounding (organs/grounding.js, ground-cite.js — Mozi) owns verifying any claim in this vision, or built from it, against real bytes. No current archon owns ablation-grain-pressure.js's live wiring or the cursor-addressable fold interface itself — both are named gaps, not silently assigned, until an archon is actually spawned for them following the Handle-table-plus-registry check.

The concrete next actionable steps, in the order this session's own findings license them, not in order of ambition: (1) unblock the shared Ollama /api/embed contention so build-ablation-grain-prior.mjs can complete a real run — infrastructure, not code. (2) Run eval/the-fold/ablation-pressure-calibration.mjs for real once centroids exist, and only wire ablationPressureFor live if that calibration actually licenses per-case trust, per the standing rule already in the code. (3) Replace this session's ad hoc agglomerative pocket-discovery with a properly-powered, established method (the gap statistic or a real mixture-model comparison) before trusting pocket counts on real data — the synthetic tests this session ran found the ad hoc version underpowered, honestly, not fixed. (4) Only after 1-3: begin the actual cursor-addressable fold interface — the piece that has been described three times this session and built zero times.

REVISION, same session, minutes later: the user asked for this to stop being a description and become a standing process -- committed to the repo, and a scheduled Claude Code routine (model: sonnet) set up to actually resume this work on a recurring cadence, archon ownership checked each time before any new task is claimed, rather than left as a one-time write. That routine's own config and its first scheduled run are the next two lines in this ledger, appended right after this one -- read those for what's actually standing, not just planned.

This ledger is the mechanism, not a description of one: append-only, each revision superseding the last without erasing it, exactly the discipline already used for every generated piece this session. Anyone — any session, any archon, any scheduled routine — reads the current fold of THIS document the same way any other document in this pipeline gets read, and appends a revision when something changes, rather than editing a fixed spec in place.

Grounding (organs/grounding.js, ground-cite.js — Mozi) owns verifying any claim in this vision, or built from it, against real bytes. No current archon owns ablation-grain-pressure.js's live wiring or the cursor-addressable fold interface itself — both are named gaps, not silently assigned, until an archon is actually spawned for them following the Handle-table-plus-registry check.

REVISION, 2026-09-26 (scheduled cron firing, resolving the exact question obs:18 named): tested cli/fold-at.mjs's significance output against a larger real document (gift-of-the-magi.md, 58 claims) instead of the smaller one (gpgp.md, 31 claims) that showed only two distinct values (16.54/17.54 bits) last cycle. Sampled 10 real cursors: significance spanned 11.51 to 19.83 bits, an 8.3-bit range -- genuine variance, not a constant. Checked causally, not just numerically: the lowest-scoring cursor ("she do it", 11.51 bits) uses common pronoun/verb words repeated throughout the story; the highest-scoring cursor ("hair fall rippling", 19.83 bits) uses distinctive, unique descriptive words -- exactly the expected Bayesian-surprise behavior (common = unsurprising = low bits, rare = surprising = high bits). This resolves the open question: the near-constant values measured last cycle were a real corpus-size effect (a 31-claim document has too few repeated relations/fillers for the prior to differentiate against), not a flaw in the slot design -- no code change was needed or made this revision, only the measurement itself, which the ledger's own last revision correctly identified as the thing actually owed.

The concrete next step this leaves open: significance is now confirmed real, working, and meaningfully discriminating on real material of sufficient size -- the same three named gaps from earlier revisions remain unaddressed (paradigm has no live caller to verify against; consequential-surprise's load-bearing/local partition needs a seedsOf design for holon-addressed claims; foldAt has never been tried on a document larger than ~140 points). Any of these, or a genuinely new direction, remains open for the next cycle -- none is uniquely licensed by this revision's own finding.

title: How this vision gets chased, not just stated (revised: claim-dependencies.js -- a real seedsOf design for consequential-surprise, built standalone)
text:
This ledger is the mechanism, not a description of one: append-only, each revision superseding the last without erasing it, exactly the discipline already used for every generated piece this session. Anyone — any session, any archon, any scheduled routine — reads the current fold of THIS document the same way any other document in this pipeline gets read, and appends a revision when something changes, rather than editing a fixed spec in place.

Ownership, checked against the real registries before any new work starts (per lesson #75): Chomsky (native/kernel/universal-grammar.js, eot-rich.js, english-parser.js, clause-tense.js) owns the parser/syntax substrate this session pushed on directly. Sullivan (adapters/text/morph-cues.js, existence-grain.js, eval/lavar/sullivan-*.mjs) owns morphology-by-elimination and the period-parse measurement that the parser's period-blindness should have been checked against sooner. LaVar (LAVAR.md, eval/lavar/) owns grading the reader against real material and keeping the mistake corpus this project's own honesty depends on. Grounding (organs/grounding.js, ground-cite.js — Mozi) owns verifying any claim in this vision, or built from it, against real bytes. No current archon owns ablation-grain-pressure.js's live wiring or the cursor-addressable fold interface itself — both are named gaps, not silently assigned, until an archon is actually spawned for them following the Handle-table-plus-registry check.

The concrete next actionable steps, in the order this session's own findings license them, not in order of ambition: (1) unblock the shared Ollama /api/embed contention so build-ablation-grain-prior.mjs can complete a real run — infrastructure, not code. (2) Run eval/the-fold/ablation-pressure-calibration.mjs for real once centroids exist, and only wire ablationPressureFor live if that calibration actually licenses per-case trust, per the standing rule already in the code. (3) Replace this session's ad hoc agglomerative pocket-discovery with a properly-powered, established method (the gap statistic or a real mixture-model comparison) before trusting pocket counts on real data — the synthetic tests this session ran found the ad hoc version underpowered, honestly, not fixed. (4) Only after 1-3: begin the actual cursor-addressable fold interface — the piece that has been described three times this session and built zero times.

REVISION, same session, minutes later: the user asked for this to stop being a description and become a standing process -- committed to the repo, and a scheduled Claude Code routine (model: sonnet) set up to actually resume this work on a recurring cadence, archon ownership checked each time before any new task is claimed, rather than left as a one-time write. That routine's own config and its first scheduled run are the next two lines in this ledger, appended right after this one -- read those for what's actually standing, not just planned.

REVISION, 2026-09-25/26: step 3 of the ordered next-steps list above is done -- native/adapters/text/pocket-discovery-gap.js implements the gap statistic (Tibshirani, Walther & Hastie 2001) replacing the ad hoc agglomerative-z-test approach, whose own honest earlier measurement this session found underpowered (1/5 true positives on realistic 3-cluster synthetic data). Measured on the SAME synthetic scenarios: 4/5 true positives (vs 1/5) at a cost of 1/5 false positives on null data (vs 0/5) -- a real, reported precision/recall trade-off, not an unqualified win. 5 node:test cases pass (native/adapters/text/pocket-discovery-gap.test.mjs). NOT wired into ablation-grain-pressure.js's buildCentroidsFrom -- steps 1-2 (unblock the shared Ollama /api/embed endpoint, run the real calibration) remain blocked; confirmed live via a 15s curl against http://127.0.0.1:11434/api/embed returning STATUS:000 immediately before this step, same failure mode observed all session. Checked both archon-ownership registries first (README.md Handle table, archon-holocracy/archons.json) -- neither names an owner for this domain, consistent with vision-routines' own prior disclosure of it as a named, undecided gap; no new archon was spawned for it this step. Committed as a standalone, tested module ahead of its dependency clearing, per the ledger's own instruction to do real, bounded, currently-licensed work rather than wait on a still-blocked step.

REVISION, 2026-09-25/26 (same 30-min-burst session): step 4 of the ordered next-steps list is BEGUN, not finished -- native/the-fold/fold-at.js is the first real slice of the cursor-addressable fold interface described repeatedly in this project's memory and built zero times before this file. foldAt(address, claims) partitions a flat GFP claim set into here/ancestors/descendants relative to a holon-address cursor, reusing kernel/gfp-claim.js's own holon()/contains()/ancestry() unmodified -- real, new plumbing, 6 node:test cases passing. The three richer layers the full vision describes (atmosphere, paradigm, significance) are deliberately left as typed gaps ({wired:false, reason}), never fabricated: atmosphere and paradigm each name a real existing module (kernel/atmosphere-math.js, the-fold/paradigm.js) this step did not wire because their real input shapes (an obligations sequence; a learned paradigm object) were not verified against a live caller; significance has no implementation anywhere in this repo at all, confirmed by grep before writing. Next bounded steps this names, not yet started: verify atmosphere-math.js's real obligations-sequence contract against a live caller and wire it in; verify paradigm.js's learnParadigm/evaluateParadigm contract and wire it in; design and build a real, null-measured significance function (no hand-set threshold, per this project's own standing rule) where none exists today. Checked both archon-ownership registries first (README.md Handle table, archon-holocracy/archons.json) for cursor/fold-at/foldat -- neither names an owner; no new archon was spawned for it this step, consistent with vision-routines' own prior disclosure of this domain as a named, undecided gap.

REVISION, 2026-09-26 (same burst session, continuing on user direction 'keep going, don't stop'): fold-at.js's atmosphere layer is now genuinely wired -- checked two real, independent production call sites first (kernel/emergent-terrain.js's atmosphereProjection, kernel/theory-of-mind.js, two separate call sites), confirmed they agree on the same obligations shape ({id, grounds, alternatives, consequences, persistence, openedAt, constraint}), then called the real interpretiveAtmosphereFactorField directly. When a caller supplies obligations, foldAt returns its real computed field; when none are supplied, atmosphere is wired:true with field:null (honestly "nothing to compute here", not "not wired"). 8 node:test cases pass (2 new, exercising both the empty and real-obligation paths). Also corrected this same ledger's own prior claim about paradigm: checking evaluateParadigm's real callers this step found ZERO outside its own test file (every real the-fold caller only ever BUILDS a paradigm via learnParadigm/learnParadigmEmergent, never evaluates a candidate against one) -- there is no live contract to verify against, so paradigm stays an honest, now more precisely worded, typed gap rather than being wired from a guess. significance remains unimplemented anywhere in the repo, re-confirmed.

REVISION, 2026-09-26 (same burst session, user: 'go, dont stop, that's the whole point of this'): corrected a FALSE claim this same file's own earlier revision made -- "no significance-measurement module exists anywhere in this repo" was wrong. Real, already-committed modules exist: kernel/bayes-surprise.js and kernel/consequential-surprise.js, both with real production callers (the-fold/expertise.js, form-prior.js, paradigm.js, learn-pass.js; kernel/settling.js, contextuality.js; organs/archon-compendium.js, capacities.js; docs/surprise-organs.js). Wired the part that fits foldAt's own PURE contract: bayes-surprise.js's predict() (read-only -- checked that admit() mutates the holograph and predict() does not, before choosing predict) computes real Bayesian surprisal in bits over slot/value facts derived from the claims at a cursor, when the caller supplies a holograph. 11 node:test cases pass total (4 new, including one that specifically proves the caller's holograph is never mutated). Left consequential-surprise.js's load-bearing/local partition as a precisely-reasoned gap -- it needs a dependents index and a seedsOf function whose real-world usage (checked via docs/surprise-organs.js) is domain-specific and does not generalize to holon-addressed claims without original design work not attempted this revision.

REVISION, 2026-09-26 (same burst session, user asked 'how close are we to arbitrary generation'): checked whether fold-at.js (built this session) connects to the nine-stage generation pipeline (native/the-fold/pipeline-run.mjs: void/surf/shape/hunt/skeleton/loop/pathos/piece). It does not -- confirmed by grep for any import of fold-at.js or any call to foldAt( anywhere under native/ outside fold-at.js and its own test file: zero matches, after catching and redoing a sloppier first grep that had produced a false hit on an unrelated function (proposition-holograph.js's foldAtom).

Looked for the most likely real integration point: hunt.js's huntGround(), since its name suggested it might already work with GFP-style ground addresses. It does not -- huntGround's "ground" is a different, unrelated concept (evidentiary source material admitted by topical relevance: naming a being of the subject, or carrying a topic word), a false friend of gfp-claim.js's holon-path "ground" that foldAt addresses. Wiring foldAt into the pipeline on the strength of shared terminology alone would have been exactly the guessed-composition mistake this session has repeatedly caught itself making and corrected (paradigm's contract, significance's non-existence claim) -- so it was not attempted. Real integration requires reading each pipeline stage's actual data model to find where a genuine holon-addressed claim set already exists or naturally could, which this step did not have room to do carefully. Named as the concrete next step, not guessed at: before wiring foldAt into generation, first identify which pipeline stage (if any) already produces or consumes GFP claims with real holon grounds, as opposed to the pipeline's own paragraph/text-based addressing.

REVISION, 2026-09-26 (same burst session, continuing 'keep going'): the prior revision correctly found hunt.js's "ground" was a false friend, but searched too narrowly before concluding no real integration point exists. Widening the check (grep for gfp-claim.js usage across every stage file pipeline-run.mjs imports) found one: native/the-fold/arrange.js imports renderGeneralization from kernel/gfp-claim.js, and arrange.js itself imports thesisBasin/thesisGeneralization from native/the-fold/thesis-claim.js -- which is the real source. thesis-claim.js builds real GFP claims with genuine holon grounds keyed to the piece's own structure: `claimFromTriple(note.end1, rel, note.end2, { ground: holon(\`/\${f.pt.part}\`), ... })` (line 136) -- one holon address per piece-part, exactly the addressing scheme foldAt consumes, not a false friend this time: verified by reading the actual line, not inferred from a name. This is confirmed, not yet wired -- thesisGen.claims is a real, holon-addressed claim set that a real caller (arrange.js) already holds at generation time; foldAt(someCursor, thesisGen.claims) would be a genuine, non-guessed integration once arrange.js's own ~650-line control flow is read carefully enough to find the right place to call it and use the result for something real (not a decorative addition). That careful read is the concrete next step, named rather than rushed into within this same burst.

REVISION, 2026-09-26 (same burst session, same 'keep going' thread): reading arrange.js's own actual control flow (not just its imports) around thesisGeneralization found a real, important caveat to the immediately prior revision. arrange.js's own comments report: "Measured 2026-09-25 across NINE real grounds — a house doc, two UD treebank READMEs, an OHS audit, a Call of the Wild excerpt, UK legislation, a SCOTUS oral-argument excerpt, the surf white paper, the Cumberland essay: zero basins validate" and, restated later in the same file, "Measured 2026-09-25 across nine real grounds (above): zero basins fired." The thesis-generalization branch that produces holon-grounded GFP claims (thesis-claim.js) is real code with a real, verified contract, but is ALSO measured, by this repo's own prior work, to never actually activate on the nine real documents tested so far. Wiring foldAt to thesisGen.claims would be technically correct and would still be honest, verified plumbing -- but by the repo's own numbers it would have nothing to act on in the overwhelming majority of real runs. This is not a reason to abandon the integration (the mechanism firing is itself measured, not assumed broken -- refrains DO trigger it per the same comments), but it tempers "found the real integration point" into "found a real, rarely-populated one" -- an honest correction, not a reversal. No wiring was attempted this revision; the next step is unchanged (arrange.js's full control flow, read carefully) but now carries this caveat forward rather than an unqualified "this is the answer."

REVISION, 2026-09-26 (scheduled cron firing, step chosen per the ledger's own named next-step): built native/the-fold/arrange.js's claimsFromFeat(feat), the general bridge from arrangeEssay's own always-run per-point extraction (feat, notesOf -- run over EVERY point in EVERY arrangeEssay call, unconditionally, verified by reading points' construction) to real, holon-addressed GFP claims, superseding the near-dormant thesis-generalization path as the practical integration point. Reuses notesOf's own already-computed subject/relation/object triples and declared polarity via claimFromTriple; notes with notesOf's own unresolved ('?') polarity state are excluded and counted separately, never coerced into a guessed '+'/'-' (gfpClaim's own validation only accepts those two, checked against its source). A pure addition -- no existing line in arrange.js changed. 6 new tests pass, including a genuine cross-file end-to-end check (claimsFromFeat's own output fed directly into the real foldAt(), confirming a parent-part claim surfaces as an ancestor for a child cursor) -- not mocked, not asserted, run. Full existing test suites (arrange-falsify.test.mjs's 32 cases, fold-at.test.mjs's 11) re-run and still pass: this addition changed nothing else. Re-tested Ollama at the top of this cycle: still STATUS:000, steps 1-2 remain blocked. Checked both archon-ownership registries for arrange.js before touching it: neither names an owner. The concrete next step this names: run claimsFromFeat against a REAL arrangeEssay call on real material (not just synthetic feat shapes) to measure how often it actually produces claims on real documents, the way thesis-claim.js's own dormancy was measured -- not yet done this revision.

REVISION, 2026-09-26 (scheduled cron firing, the exact next step obs:12 named): ran claimsFromFeat against REAL arrangeEssay output on real prose, not synthetic feat shapes, through the actual pipeline (buildDraft/attachReferents/loadEotParser/attachEot/arrangeEssay). Measured on three real documents already used in this session's own summarization pilot: gpgp.md (Wikipedia, informational) 31 claims from 52 points, 0 unresolved; gift-of-the-magi.md (O. Henry, narrative) 58 claims from 140 points, 3 unresolved; war-and-peace-ch45.md (Tolstoy, translated 19th-century prose) 14 claims from 44 points, 1 unresolved. All three real, nonzero, non-degenerate -- confirming claimsFromFeat is commonly populated on real material, the opposite of thesis-claim.js's own measured zero-activation result. Exposed claimsFromFeat's output on arrangeEssay's own return value (a new `claims` key, additive only -- checked for any deep-equality assertion against a whole outline object anywhere in the repo before adding it; none found) so a real caller can reach it without reaching into arrangeEssay's function-local `feat`. Locked in as a committed, reproducible test (claims-from-feat-real.test.mjs, a real public-domain excerpt embedded directly rather than depending on this session's own scratchpad paths, unlike the pre-existing native/eval/the-fold/drive-summary-experiment.mjs's own default file paths -- a fragility noted, not fixed, this revision). Full existing suites re-verified: 44 tests across arrange-falsify.test.mjs, claims-from-feat.test.mjs and fold-at.test.mjs still pass. Re-tested Ollama at the top of this cycle: still STATUS:000, steps 1-2 remain blocked. The concrete next step this names: something must actually CALL arrangeEssay's new claims field and DO something with it via foldAt (atmosphere/significance) that changes what the pipeline produces -- until then this is verified, reachable data, not yet a capability.

REVISION, 2026-09-26 (scheduled cron firing): before wiring foldAt's output into anything that shapes generated text (obs:13's own named next step), tried calling foldAt against the real claims measured last cycle to see what it actually returns. Found ancestors:0, descendants:0 for every real cursor tried against gpgp.md's 31 claims -- the ground claimsFromFeat builds, holon(`/${f.pt.part}`), is FLAT (e.g. '/p18'), so every claim sits as a sibling of every other at the same depth; foldAt's ancestor/descendant machinery had nothing to find, regardless of how much real content existed. Checked eot-draft.js's own point construction (line 187) and found every point already carries a real, pre-existing hierarchical `path` field (`whole/p${i+1}/${j+1}`, e.g. 'whole/p4/3') that arrange.js's own points construction (line 121, `{...pt, part: p.id}`) already preserves onto every feat entry as `f.pt.path` -- unused until now. Fixed: claimsFromFeat's ground is now `holon(f.pt.path ?? \`/${f.pt.part}\`)`, using the real hierarchy with a fallback for any caller whose feat entries lack `path`. Re-ran the same live inspection against gpgp.md: grounds are now genuinely nested ('/whole/p13/3', '/whole/p16/2', ...), confirmed real, not just plausible-looking.

Disclosed, not solved: even with the real hierarchy, ancestors/descendants for a point-level cursor remain empty in this design, because no claim is currently grounded at the coarser part ('/whole/pN') or whole-document level -- points are real siblings under a shared part, not ancestor/descendant of each other, and foldAt has no separate "siblings" category. Getting real ancestor context (not just a correct address) needs either claims at multiple granularities or a sibling-aware fourth category in foldAt itself -- named as the next concrete step, not attempted this revision. 2 new tests lock in the fix (path used when present; flat fallback unchanged when absent); full suite re-verified at 47/47 passing across claims-from-feat, claims-from-feat-real, arrange-falsify and fold-at test files. Re-tested Ollama at the top of this cycle: still down, steps 1-2 remain blocked.

REVISION, 2026-09-26 (scheduled cron firing, the exact gap obs:14 named): added a fourth, purely structural category to foldAt -- siblings: claims sharing the cursor's own parent holon (one level up, via gfp-claim.js's own already-exported segmentsOf/holon, no new addressing concept). This directly answers what obs:14 found and disclosed: real per-point claims from claimsFromFeat are true siblings of each other under a shared part, not ancestor/descendant, and foldAt had no category for that relationship. Re-ran the same live inspection against gpgp.md's real claims that found the original gap: a cursor at /whole/p16/2 now correctly returns /whole/p16/1 as a real sibling -- confirmed on real data, not just the synthetic fixture. parentOf(h) returns null for the root ('/' has no parent), so the root cursor correctly has zero siblings, a real structural fact rather than an arbitrary special case. 3 new tests added (sibling inclusion, no double-counting an ancestor as a sibling, root has zero siblings); full suite re-verified at 49/49 passing across fold-at, claims-from-feat, claims-from-feat-real and arrange-falsify test files. Re-tested Ollama at the top of this cycle: still down, steps 1-2 remain blocked. The concrete next step this names: foldAt now has real, populated here/ancestors/siblings on real material -- the next honest question is whether wiring this into a generation-shaping stage (finish.js, loop-check.js) actually improves anything measurable, since no existing gap in either file currently names a use for it (checked two cycles ago); that measurement, not another foldAt feature, is what's actually owed next.

REVISION, 2026-09-26 (scheduled cron firing, pursuing obs:15's own named question): before writing more foldAt code, tried to find a REAL, already-motivated use for its siblings/ancestors in a generation-shaping stage, rather than inventing one. Read three candidate files' actual logic (not just names or comments): hunt.js's huntGround (already found, two cycles ago, to be a false-friend "ground" concept -- evidentiary source material, unrelated); finish.js's takesUp (checks whether a part's opening sentence "takes up" a being or word from the previous part's closing sentence -- works entirely through referent resolution and word overlap on raw text, never touches a GFP claim); loop-check.js's measurePiece/judgeLoop (measures whether a loop preserved anchors and answered the task's questions -- works through anchorsFor/carries on the piece's own text, never a GFP claim either). None of the three has an unmet need that foldAt's holon-addressed claim context would fill; each already solves its own adjacency/coherence problem through a different, working, non-claim-based mechanism. Wiring foldAt into any of them now would be manufacturing a use for it, not fulfilling one already there -- exactly the invented-purpose mistake this session's own standing rule (measure, don't assume) exists to catch.

This is not a dead end for foldAt, but it does redirect the real next step: either (a) foldAt's value is as a genuinely NEW capability (an interactive query/inspection surface over already-generated material, not a silent improvement folded into logic that already works its own way), which has never been attempted and would need its own honest scoping, not a forced retrofit; or (b) a deliberately DESIGNED experiment -- pick one specific generation decision, build a foldAt-informed alternative, and measure it against the current approach on real material -- which is a real, bounded project of its own, not something to back into by searching existing files for an accidental fit. Which of these two paths is worth pursuing is an open decision this revision names but does not make.

REVISION, 2026-09-26 (scheduled cron firing, pursuing obs:16's own named option (a)): built cli/fold-at.mjs, the first time anything in this repo lets a person actually run a command and ask "what is the fold at this point" of a real document, rather than only exercising the backend through a test or a throwaway script. Runs the real pipeline (buildDraft, attachReferents, loadEotParser, attachEot, arrangeEssay) on a file argument, then the real foldAt(address, outline.claims), printing here/ancestors/siblings/descendants and each layer's real state -- a computed field when wired, the exact honest gap reason string when not, never a fabricated summary. A `list` address mode prints every real distinct holon address the document actually produced, so a user finds a real cursor rather than guessing one. Verified against a real document (gpgp.md): 31 claims, 31 addresses listed correctly; querying /whole/p16/2 correctly returned its real sibling at /whole/p16/1 and honest gap text for significance and paradigm. 3 process-level tests (spawning the real CLI, not importing its internals) lock this in, covering usage/exit-2, list mode, and a real address query's full output shape. This is the "genuinely new capability" path named as option (a) two cycles ago, chosen over forcing a retrofit into pipeline stages already found to have no motivating gap for it.

REVISION, 2026-09-26 (scheduled cron firing): the CLI's significance output previously always printed "gap: no holograph supplied" since nothing built one. Fixed: cli/fold-at.mjs now builds a real bayes-surprise.js holograph, admitting (via the real, documented-mutating admit()) every OTHER claim in the document (excluding the queried cursor's own, to avoid a self-fulfilling low score), using the same slotsFromClaims() shape foldAt itself already uses internally (exported from fold-at.js for this purpose -- a one-word, no-behavior-change export). foldAt then reports the cursor's real surprisal against this real, document-derived prior via its own existing predict()-only path (never re-admitting).

Honestly measured, not just built: tested against gpgp.md's 4 different real cursors -- significance came back as either 16.54 or 17.54 bits, only two distinct values across four tries. The likely cause, checked by reading slotsFromClaims' own slot-naming: every claim's role fillers compete in the SAME small set of shared slots (rel, role:ARG0, role:ARG1, polarity) across the whole 31-claim document, and most specific fillers (proper nouns, specific nouns) are unique to the document, so the "novel value" cost in bayes-surprise.js's own Bayesian model dominates almost uniformly regardless of which claim is queried. This is a real, working number, not fabricated -- but it does not yet meaningfully discriminate "surprising" from "unsurprising" content on a corpus this small, and should not be presented as more informative than it is. 2 new tests (fold-at.js's export, the CLI's real-number output) plus the full existing suite re-verified passing (16 fold-at + 4 cli tests). Re-tested Ollama: still down.

The next honest question this names: does significance become more discriminating on a larger real document (war-and-peace-ch45.md, or the full text rather than an excerpt), or is a coarser slot design (grouping by relation LEMMA across claims, not per-claim-instance) needed regardless of size -- not yet tested, named as the next step rather than assumed either way.

REVISION, 2026-09-26 (scheduled cron firing, resolving the exact question obs:18 named): tested cli/fold-at.mjs's significance output against a larger real document (gift-of-the-magi.md, 58 claims) instead of the smaller one (gpgp.md, 31 claims) that showed only two distinct values (16.54/17.54 bits) last cycle. Sampled 10 real cursors: significance spanned 11.51 to 19.83 bits, an 8.3-bit range -- genuine variance, not a constant. Checked causally, not just numerically: the lowest-scoring cursor ("she do it", 11.51 bits) uses common pronoun/verb words repeated throughout the story; the highest-scoring cursor ("hair fall rippling", 19.83 bits) uses distinctive, unique descriptive words -- exactly the expected Bayesian-surprise behavior (common = unsurprising = low bits, rare = surprising = high bits). This resolves the open question: the near-constant values measured last cycle were a real corpus-size effect (a 31-claim document has too few repeated relations/fillers for the prior to differentiate against), not a flaw in the slot design -- no code change was needed or made this revision, only the measurement itself, which the ledger's own last revision correctly identified as the thing actually owed.

The concrete next step this leaves open: significance is now confirmed real, working, and meaningfully discriminating on real material of sufficient size -- the same three named gaps from earlier revisions remain unaddressed (paradigm has no live caller to verify against; consequential-surprise's load-bearing/local partition needs a seedsOf design for holon-addressed claims; foldAt has never been tried on a document larger than ~140 points). Any of these, or a genuinely new direction, remains open for the next cycle -- none is uniquely licensed by this revision's own finding.

REVISION, 2026-09-26 (scheduled cron firing, picking one of the three open options from obs:19 -- consequential-surprise.js's own named gap): built native/the-fold/claim-dependencies.js, the missing seedsOf/dependents-index design for wiring kernel/consequential-surprise.js's load-bearing/local significance partition into holon-addressed GFP claims. Before building, checked ownership carefully and found a real, non-obvious false-friend: an archon's mission mentions "cascade," but its own text names native/kernel/prior-query.js's unrelated "meaning-potential cascade" (a chain of prior-family lookups), not kernel/cascade.js (BFS reachability over a dependency graph) -- confirmed by reading prior-query.js directly; kernel/cascade.js itself has zero references in either registry, genuinely unowned.

The dependency relation: two claims are connected when they share a role filler (the same ARG0 or ARG1 value) -- a mechanical proxy for shared-entity/coreference connection, consistent with how this project already treats shared referents elsewhere (finish.js's takesUp, referents.js's resolved beings), not a newly invented notion. claimDependencyIndex(claims) builds kernel/cascade.js's own dependentsIndex from this relation; seedsOfClaimFiller(slot, value) seeds only from role-shaped slots (matching fold-at.js's own slotsFromClaims naming), never from rel or polarity, which carry no shareable entity. 4 tests pass, including one against real claims from gpgp.md confirming real role fillers are genuinely shared across more than one real claim, not just true on synthetic data. Full existing suite re-verified: 25 tests across fold-at, claims-from-feat and cli/fold-at, no regressions.

Built and tested standalone only -- NOT yet wired into fold-at.js's significance field or the CLI, which remains the next concrete step: call consequentialSurprise(holo, facts, {index, seedsOf: seedsOfClaimFiller, ...}) inside foldAt when the caller supplies an index (built via claimDependencyIndex), alongside the existing predict()-only path, and measure whether it produces a genuinely different (and genuinely load-bearing) partition on real material -- not attempted this revision. Re-tested Ollama: still down.
basis: Landed by the scheduled 30-minute cron routine, picking the consequential-surprise seedsOf gap from the three options the ledger's own prior revision left open. Checked ownership carefully enough to catch a real false-friend collision before concluding the domain was free to build in.

title: How this vision gets chased, not just stated (revised: consequential-surprise wired for real, preserving foldAt's own purity via a real holograph clone)
text:
This ledger is the mechanism, not a description of one: append-only, each revision superseding the last without erasing it, exactly the discipline already used for every generated piece this session. Anyone — any session, any archon, any scheduled routine — reads the current fold of THIS document the same way any other document in this pipeline gets read, and appends a revision when something changes, rather than editing a fixed spec in place.

Ownership, checked against the real registries before any new work starts (per lesson #75): Chomsky (native/kernel/universal-grammar.js, eot-rich.js, english-parser.js, clause-tense.js) owns the parser/syntax substrate this session pushed on directly. Sullivan (adapters/text/morph-cues.js, existence-grain.js, eval/lavar/sullivan-*.mjs) owns morphology-by-elimination and the period-parse measurement that the parser's period-blindness should have been checked against sooner. LaVar (LAVAR.md, eval/lavar/) owns grading the reader against real material and keeping the mistake corpus this project's own honesty depends on. Grounding (organs/grounding.js, ground-cite.js — Mozi) owns verifying any claim in this vision, or built from it, against real bytes. No current archon owns ablation-grain-pressure.js's live wiring or the cursor-addressable fold interface itself — both are named gaps, not silently assigned, until an archon is actually spawned for them following the Handle-table-plus-registry check.

The concrete next actionable steps, in the order this session's own findings license them, not in order of ambition: (1) unblock the shared Ollama /api/embed contention so build-ablation-grain-prior.mjs can complete a real run — infrastructure, not code. (2) Run eval/the-fold/ablation-pressure-calibration.mjs for real once centroids exist, and only wire ablationPressureFor live if that calibration actually licenses per-case trust, per the standing rule already in the code. (3) Replace this session's ad hoc agglomerative pocket-discovery with a properly-powered, established method (the gap statistic or a real mixture-model comparison) before trusting pocket counts on real data — the synthetic tests this session ran found the ad hoc version underpowered, honestly, not fixed. (4) Only after 1-3: begin the actual cursor-addressable fold interface — the piece that has been described three times this session and built zero times.

REVISION, same session, minutes later: the user asked for this to stop being a description and become a standing process -- committed to the repo, and a scheduled Claude Code routine (model: sonnet) set up to actually resume this work on a recurring cadence, archon ownership checked each time before any new task is claimed, rather than left as a one-time write. That routine's own config and its first scheduled run are the next two lines in this ledger, appended right after this one -- read those for what's actually standing, not just planned.

REVISION, 2026-09-25/26: step 3 of the ordered next-steps list above is done -- native/adapters/text/pocket-discovery-gap.js implements the gap statistic (Tibshirani, Walther & Hastie 2001) replacing the ad hoc agglomerative-z-test approach, whose own honest earlier measurement this session found underpowered (1/5 true positives on realistic 3-cluster synthetic data). Measured on the SAME synthetic scenarios: 4/5 true positives (vs 1/5) at a cost of 1/5 false positives on null data (vs 0/5) -- a real, reported precision/recall trade-off, not an unqualified win. 5 node:test cases pass (native/adapters/text/pocket-discovery-gap.test.mjs). NOT wired into ablation-grain-pressure.js's buildCentroidsFrom -- steps 1-2 (unblock the shared Ollama /api/embed endpoint, run the real calibration) remain blocked; confirmed live via a 15s curl against http://127.0.0.1:11434/api/embed returning STATUS:000 immediately before this step, same failure mode observed all session. Checked both archon-ownership registries first (README.md Handle table, archon-holocracy/archons.json) -- neither names an owner for this domain, consistent with vision-routines' own prior disclosure of it as a named, undecided gap; no new archon was spawned for it this step. Committed as a standalone, tested module ahead of its dependency clearing, per the ledger's own instruction to do real, bounded, currently-licensed work rather than wait on a still-blocked step.

REVISION, 2026-09-25/26 (same 30-min-burst session): step 4 of the ordered next-steps list is BEGUN, not finished -- native/the-fold/fold-at.js is the first real slice of the cursor-addressable fold interface described repeatedly in this project's memory and built zero times before this file. foldAt(address, claims) partitions a flat GFP claim set into here/ancestors/descendants relative to a holon-address cursor, reusing kernel/gfp-claim.js's own holon()/contains()/ancestry() unmodified -- real, new plumbing, 6 node:test cases passing. The three richer layers the full vision describes (atmosphere, paradigm, significance) are deliberately left as typed gaps ({wired:false, reason}), never fabricated: atmosphere and paradigm each name a real existing module (kernel/atmosphere-math.js, the-fold/paradigm.js) this step did not wire because their real input shapes (an obligations sequence; a learned paradigm object) were not verified against a live caller; significance has no implementation anywhere in this repo at all, confirmed by grep before writing. Next bounded steps this names, not yet started: verify atmosphere-math.js's real obligations-sequence contract against a live caller and wire it in; verify paradigm.js's learnParadigm/evaluateParadigm contract and wire it in; design and build a real, null-measured significance function (no hand-set threshold, per this project's own standing rule) where none exists today. Checked both archon-ownership registries first (README.md Handle table, archon-holocracy/archons.json) for cursor/fold-at/foldat -- neither names an owner; no new archon was spawned for it this step, consistent with vision-routines' own prior disclosure of this domain as a named, undecided gap.

REVISION, 2026-09-26 (same burst session, continuing on user direction 'keep going, don't stop'): fold-at.js's atmosphere layer is now genuinely wired -- checked two real, independent production call sites first (kernel/emergent-terrain.js's atmosphereProjection, kernel/theory-of-mind.js, two separate call sites), confirmed they agree on the same obligations shape ({id, grounds, alternatives, consequences, persistence, openedAt, constraint}), then called the real interpretiveAtmosphereFactorField directly. When a caller supplies obligations, foldAt returns its real computed field; when none are supplied, atmosphere is wired:true with field:null (honestly "nothing to compute here", not "not wired"). 8 node:test cases pass (2 new, exercising both the empty and real-obligation paths). Also corrected this same ledger's own prior claim about paradigm: checking evaluateParadigm's real callers this step found ZERO outside its own test file (every real the-fold caller only ever BUILDS a paradigm via learnParadigm/learnParadigmEmergent, never evaluates a candidate against one) -- there is no live contract to verify against, so paradigm stays an honest, now more precisely worded, typed gap rather than being wired from a guess. significance remains unimplemented anywhere in the repo, re-confirmed.

REVISION, 2026-09-26 (same burst session, user: 'go, dont stop, that's the whole point of this'): corrected a FALSE claim this same file's own earlier revision made -- "no significance-measurement module exists anywhere in this repo" was wrong. Real, already-committed modules exist: kernel/bayes-surprise.js and kernel/consequential-surprise.js, both with real production callers (the-fold/expertise.js, form-prior.js, paradigm.js, learn-pass.js; kernel/settling.js, contextuality.js; organs/archon-compendium.js, capacities.js; docs/surprise-organs.js). Wired the part that fits foldAt's own PURE contract: bayes-surprise.js's predict() (read-only -- checked that admit() mutates the holograph and predict() does not, before choosing predict) computes real Bayesian surprisal in bits over slot/value facts derived from the claims at a cursor, when the caller supplies a holograph. 11 node:test cases pass total (4 new, including one that specifically proves the caller's holograph is never mutated). Left consequential-surprise.js's load-bearing/local partition as a precisely-reasoned gap -- it needs a dependents index and a seedsOf function whose real-world usage (checked via docs/surprise-organs.js) is domain-specific and does not generalize to holon-addressed claims without original design work not attempted this revision.

REVISION, 2026-09-26 (same burst session, user asked 'how close are we to arbitrary generation'): checked whether fold-at.js (built this session) connects to the nine-stage generation pipeline (native/the-fold/pipeline-run.mjs: void/surf/shape/hunt/skeleton/loop/pathos/piece). It does not -- confirmed by grep for any import of fold-at.js or any call to foldAt( anywhere under native/ outside fold-at.js and its own test file: zero matches, after catching and redoing a sloppier first grep that had produced a false hit on an unrelated function (proposition-holograph.js's foldAtom).

Looked for the most likely real integration point: hunt.js's huntGround(), since its name suggested it might already work with GFP-style ground addresses. It does not -- huntGround's "ground" is a different, unrelated concept (evidentiary source material admitted by topical relevance: naming a being of the subject, or carrying a topic word), a false friend of gfp-claim.js's holon-path "ground" that foldAt addresses. Wiring foldAt into the pipeline on the strength of shared terminology alone would have been exactly the guessed-composition mistake this session has repeatedly caught itself making and corrected (paradigm's contract, significance's non-existence claim) -- so it was not attempted. Real integration requires reading each pipeline stage's actual data model to find where a genuine holon-addressed claim set already exists or naturally could, which this step did not have room to do carefully. Named as the concrete next step, not guessed at: before wiring foldAt into generation, first identify which pipeline stage (if any) already produces or consumes GFP claims with real holon grounds, as opposed to the pipeline's own paragraph/text-based addressing.

REVISION, 2026-09-26 (same burst session, continuing 'keep going'): the prior revision correctly found hunt.js's "ground" was a false friend, but searched too narrowly before concluding no real integration point exists. Widening the check (grep for gfp-claim.js usage across every stage file pipeline-run.mjs imports) found one: native/the-fold/arrange.js imports renderGeneralization from kernel/gfp-claim.js, and arrange.js itself imports thesisBasin/thesisGeneralization from native/the-fold/thesis-claim.js -- which is the real source. thesis-claim.js builds real GFP claims with genuine holon grounds keyed to the piece's own structure: `claimFromTriple(note.end1, rel, note.end2, { ground: holon(\`/\${f.pt.part}\`), ... })` (line 136) -- one holon address per piece-part, exactly the addressing scheme foldAt consumes, not a false friend this time: verified by reading the actual line, not inferred from a name. This is confirmed, not yet wired -- thesisGen.claims is a real, holon-addressed claim set that a real caller (arrange.js) already holds at generation time; foldAt(someCursor, thesisGen.claims) would be a genuine, non-guessed integration once arrange.js's own ~650-line control flow is read carefully enough to find the right place to call it and use the result for something real (not a decorative addition). That careful read is the concrete next step, named rather than rushed into within this same burst.

REVISION, 2026-09-26 (same burst session, same 'keep going' thread): reading arrange.js's own actual control flow (not just its imports) around thesisGeneralization found a real, important caveat to the immediately prior revision. arrange.js's own comments report: "Measured 2026-09-25 across NINE real grounds — a house doc, two UD treebank READMEs, an OHS audit, a Call of the Wild excerpt, UK legislation, a SCOTUS oral-argument excerpt, the surf white paper, the Cumberland essay: zero basins validate" and, restated later in the same file, "Measured 2026-09-25 across nine real grounds (above): zero basins fired." The thesis-generalization branch that produces holon-grounded GFP claims (thesis-claim.js) is real code with a real, verified contract, but is ALSO measured, by this repo's own prior work, to never actually activate on the nine real documents tested so far. Wiring foldAt to thesisGen.claims would be technically correct and would still be honest, verified plumbing -- but by the repo's own numbers it would have nothing to act on in the overwhelming majority of real runs. This is not a reason to abandon the integration (the mechanism firing is itself measured, not assumed broken -- refrains DO trigger it per the same comments), but it tempers "found the real integration point" into "found a real, rarely-populated one" -- an honest correction, not a reversal. No wiring was attempted this revision; the next step is unchanged (arrange.js's full control flow, read carefully) but now carries this caveat forward rather than an unqualified "this is the answer."

REVISION, 2026-09-26 (scheduled cron firing, step chosen per the ledger's own named next-step): built native/the-fold/arrange.js's claimsFromFeat(feat), the general bridge from arrangeEssay's own always-run per-point extraction (feat, notesOf -- run over EVERY point in EVERY arrangeEssay call, unconditionally, verified by reading points' construction) to real, holon-addressed GFP claims, superseding the near-dormant thesis-generalization path as the practical integration point. Reuses notesOf's own already-computed subject/relation/object triples and declared polarity via claimFromTriple; notes with notesOf's own unresolved ('?') polarity state are excluded and counted separately, never coerced into a guessed '+'/'-' (gfpClaim's own validation only accepts those two, checked against its source). A pure addition -- no existing line in arrange.js changed. 6 new tests pass, including a genuine cross-file end-to-end check (claimsFromFeat's own output fed directly into the real foldAt(), confirming a parent-part claim surfaces as an ancestor for a child cursor) -- not mocked, not asserted, run. Full existing test suites (arrange-falsify.test.mjs's 32 cases, fold-at.test.mjs's 11) re-run and still pass: this addition changed nothing else. Re-tested Ollama at the top of this cycle: still STATUS:000, steps 1-2 remain blocked. Checked both archon-ownership registries for arrange.js before touching it: neither names an owner. The concrete next step this names: run claimsFromFeat against a REAL arrangeEssay call on real material (not just synthetic feat shapes) to measure how often it actually produces claims on real documents, the way thesis-claim.js's own dormancy was measured -- not yet done this revision.

REVISION, 2026-09-26 (scheduled cron firing, the exact next step obs:12 named): ran claimsFromFeat against REAL arrangeEssay output on real prose, not synthetic feat shapes, through the actual pipeline (buildDraft/attachReferents/loadEotParser/attachEot/arrangeEssay). Measured on three real documents already used in this session's own summarization pilot: gpgp.md (Wikipedia, informational) 31 claims from 52 points, 0 unresolved; gift-of-the-magi.md (O. Henry, narrative) 58 claims from 140 points, 3 unresolved; war-and-peace-ch45.md (Tolstoy, translated 19th-century prose) 14 claims from 44 points, 1 unresolved. All three real, nonzero, non-degenerate -- confirming claimsFromFeat is commonly populated on real material, the opposite of thesis-claim.js's own measured zero-activation result. Exposed claimsFromFeat's output on arrangeEssay's own return value (a new `claims` key, additive only -- checked for any deep-equality assertion against a whole outline object anywhere in the repo before adding it; none found) so a real caller can reach it without reaching into arrangeEssay's function-local `feat`. Locked in as a committed, reproducible test (claims-from-feat-real.test.mjs, a real public-domain excerpt embedded directly rather than depending on this session's own scratchpad paths, unlike the pre-existing native/eval/the-fold/drive-summary-experiment.mjs's own default file paths -- a fragility noted, not fixed, this revision). Full existing suites re-verified: 44 tests across arrange-falsify.test.mjs, claims-from-feat.test.mjs and fold-at.test.mjs still pass. Re-tested Ollama at the top of this cycle: still STATUS:000, steps 1-2 remain blocked. The concrete next step this names: something must actually CALL arrangeEssay's new claims field and DO something with it via foldAt (atmosphere/significance) that changes what the pipeline produces -- until then this is verified, reachable data, not yet a capability.

REVISION, 2026-09-26 (scheduled cron firing): before wiring foldAt's output into anything that shapes generated text (obs:13's own named next step), tried calling foldAt against the real claims measured last cycle to see what it actually returns. Found ancestors:0, descendants:0 for every real cursor tried against gpgp.md's 31 claims -- the ground claimsFromFeat builds, holon(`/${f.pt.part}`), is FLAT (e.g. '/p18'), so every claim sits as a sibling of every other at the same depth; foldAt's ancestor/descendant machinery had nothing to find, regardless of how much real content existed. Checked eot-draft.js's own point construction (line 187) and found every point already carries a real, pre-existing hierarchical `path` field (`whole/p${i+1}/${j+1}`, e.g. 'whole/p4/3') that arrange.js's own points construction (line 121, `{...pt, part: p.id}`) already preserves onto every feat entry as `f.pt.path` -- unused until now. Fixed: claimsFromFeat's ground is now `holon(f.pt.path ?? \`/${f.pt.part}\`)`, using the real hierarchy with a fallback for any caller whose feat entries lack `path`. Re-ran the same live inspection against gpgp.md: grounds are now genuinely nested ('/whole/p13/3', '/whole/p16/2', ...), confirmed real, not just plausible-looking.

Disclosed, not solved: even with the real hierarchy, ancestors/descendants for a point-level cursor remain empty in this design, because no claim is currently grounded at the coarser part ('/whole/pN') or whole-document level -- points are real siblings under a shared part, not ancestor/descendant of each other, and foldAt has no separate "siblings" category. Getting real ancestor context (not just a correct address) needs either claims at multiple granularities or a sibling-aware fourth category in foldAt itself -- named as the next concrete step, not attempted this revision. 2 new tests lock in the fix (path used when present; flat fallback unchanged when absent); full suite re-verified at 47/47 passing across claims-from-feat, claims-from-feat-real, arrange-falsify and fold-at test files. Re-tested Ollama at the top of this cycle: still down, steps 1-2 remain blocked.

REVISION, 2026-09-26 (scheduled cron firing, the exact gap obs:14 named): added a fourth, purely structural category to foldAt -- siblings: claims sharing the cursor's own parent holon (one level up, via gfp-claim.js's own already-exported segmentsOf/holon, no new addressing concept). This directly answers what obs:14 found and disclosed: real per-point claims from claimsFromFeat are true siblings of each other under a shared part, not ancestor/descendant, and foldAt had no category for that relationship. Re-ran the same live inspection against gpgp.md's real claims that found the original gap: a cursor at /whole/p16/2 now correctly returns /whole/p16/1 as a real sibling -- confirmed on real data, not just the synthetic fixture. parentOf(h) returns null for the root ('/' has no parent), so the root cursor correctly has zero siblings, a real structural fact rather than an arbitrary special case. 3 new tests added (sibling inclusion, no double-counting an ancestor as a sibling, root has zero siblings); full suite re-verified at 49/49 passing across fold-at, claims-from-feat, claims-from-feat-real and arrange-falsify test files. Re-tested Ollama at the top of this cycle: still down, steps 1-2 remain blocked. The concrete next step this names: foldAt now has real, populated here/ancestors/siblings on real material -- the next honest question is whether wiring this into a generation-shaping stage (finish.js, loop-check.js) actually improves anything measurable, since no existing gap in either file currently names a use for it (checked two cycles ago); that measurement, not another foldAt feature, is what's actually owed next.

REVISION, 2026-09-26 (scheduled cron firing, pursuing obs:15's own named question): before writing more foldAt code, tried to find a REAL, already-motivated use for its siblings/ancestors in a generation-shaping stage, rather than inventing one. Read three candidate files' actual logic (not just names or comments): hunt.js's huntGround (already found, two cycles ago, to be a false-friend "ground" concept -- evidentiary source material, unrelated); finish.js's takesUp (checks whether a part's opening sentence "takes up" a being or word from the previous part's closing sentence -- works entirely through referent resolution and word overlap on raw text, never touches a GFP claim); loop-check.js's measurePiece/judgeLoop (measures whether a loop preserved anchors and answered the task's questions -- works through anchorsFor/carries on the piece's own text, never a GFP claim either). None of the three has an unmet need that foldAt's holon-addressed claim context would fill; each already solves its own adjacency/coherence problem through a different, working, non-claim-based mechanism. Wiring foldAt into any of them now would be manufacturing a use for it, not fulfilling one already there -- exactly the invented-purpose mistake this session's own standing rule (measure, don't assume) exists to catch.

This is not a dead end for foldAt, but it does redirect the real next step: either (a) foldAt's value is as a genuinely NEW capability (an interactive query/inspection surface over already-generated material, not a silent improvement folded into logic that already works its own way), which has never been attempted and would need its own honest scoping, not a forced retrofit; or (b) a deliberately DESIGNED experiment -- pick one specific generation decision, build a foldAt-informed alternative, and measure it against the current approach on real material -- which is a real, bounded project of its own, not something to back into by searching existing files for an accidental fit. Which of these two paths is worth pursuing is an open decision this revision names but does not make.

REVISION, 2026-09-26 (scheduled cron firing, pursuing obs:16's own named option (a)): built cli/fold-at.mjs, the first time anything in this repo lets a person actually run a command and ask "what is the fold at this point" of a real document, rather than only exercising the backend through a test or a throwaway script. Runs the real pipeline (buildDraft, attachReferents, loadEotParser, attachEot, arrangeEssay) on a file argument, then the real foldAt(address, outline.claims), printing here/ancestors/siblings/descendants and each layer's real state -- a computed field when wired, the exact honest gap reason string when not, never a fabricated summary. A `list` address mode prints every real distinct holon address the document actually produced, so a user finds a real cursor rather than guessing one. Verified against a real document (gpgp.md): 31 claims, 31 addresses listed correctly; querying /whole/p16/2 correctly returned its real sibling at /whole/p16/1 and honest gap text for significance and paradigm. 3 process-level tests (spawning the real CLI, not importing its internals) lock this in, covering usage/exit-2, list mode, and a real address query's full output shape. This is the "genuinely new capability" path named as option (a) two cycles ago, chosen over forcing a retrofit into pipeline stages already found to have no motivating gap for it.

REVISION, 2026-09-26 (scheduled cron firing): the CLI's significance output previously always printed "gap: no holograph supplied" since nothing built one. Fixed: cli/fold-at.mjs now builds a real bayes-surprise.js holograph, admitting (via the real, documented-mutating admit()) every OTHER claim in the document (excluding the queried cursor's own, to avoid a self-fulfilling low score), using the same slotsFromClaims() shape foldAt itself already uses internally (exported from fold-at.js for this purpose -- a one-word, no-behavior-change export). foldAt then reports the cursor's real surprisal against this real, document-derived prior via its own existing predict()-only path (never re-admitting).

Honestly measured, not just built: tested against gpgp.md's 4 different real cursors -- significance came back as either 16.54 or 17.54 bits, only two distinct values across four tries. The likely cause, checked by reading slotsFromClaims' own slot-naming: every claim's role fillers compete in the SAME small set of shared slots (rel, role:ARG0, role:ARG1, polarity) across the whole 31-claim document, and most specific fillers (proper nouns, specific nouns) are unique to the document, so the "novel value" cost in bayes-surprise.js's own Bayesian model dominates almost uniformly regardless of which claim is queried. This is a real, working number, not fabricated -- but it does not yet meaningfully discriminate "surprising" from "unsurprising" content on a corpus this small, and should not be presented as more informative than it is. 2 new tests (fold-at.js's export, the CLI's real-number output) plus the full existing suite re-verified passing (16 fold-at + 4 cli tests). Re-tested Ollama: still down.

The next honest question this names: does significance become more discriminating on a larger real document (war-and-peace-ch45.md, or the full text rather than an excerpt), or is a coarser slot design (grouping by relation LEMMA across claims, not per-claim-instance) needed regardless of size -- not yet tested, named as the next step rather than assumed either way.

REVISION, 2026-09-26 (scheduled cron firing, resolving the exact question obs:18 named): tested cli/fold-at.mjs's significance output against a larger real document (gift-of-the-magi.md, 58 claims) instead of the smaller one (gpgp.md, 31 claims) that showed only two distinct values (16.54/17.54 bits) last cycle. Sampled 10 real cursors: significance spanned 11.51 to 19.83 bits, an 8.3-bit range -- genuine variance, not a constant. Checked causally, not just numerically: the lowest-scoring cursor ("she do it", 11.51 bits) uses common pronoun/verb words repeated throughout the story; the highest-scoring cursor ("hair fall rippling", 19.83 bits) uses distinctive, unique descriptive words -- exactly the expected Bayesian-surprise behavior (common = unsurprising = low bits, rare = surprising = high bits). This resolves the open question: the near-constant values measured last cycle were a real corpus-size effect (a 31-claim document has too few repeated relations/fillers for the prior to differentiate against), not a flaw in the slot design -- no code change was needed or made this revision, only the measurement itself, which the ledger's own last revision correctly identified as the thing actually owed.

The concrete next step this leaves open: significance is now confirmed real, working, and meaningfully discriminating on real material of sufficient size -- the same three named gaps from earlier revisions remain unaddressed (paradigm has no live caller to verify against; consequential-surprise's load-bearing/local partition needs a seedsOf design for holon-addressed claims; foldAt has never been tried on a document larger than ~140 points). Any of these, or a genuinely new direction, remains open for the next cycle -- none is uniquely licensed by this revision's own finding.

REVISION, 2026-09-26 (scheduled cron firing, picking one of the three open options from obs:19 -- consequential-surprise.js's own named gap): built native/the-fold/claim-dependencies.js, the missing seedsOf/dependents-index design for wiring kernel/consequential-surprise.js's load-bearing/local significance partition into holon-addressed GFP claims. Before building, checked ownership carefully and found a real, non-obvious false-friend: an archon's mission mentions "cascade," but its own text names native/kernel/prior-query.js's unrelated "meaning-potential cascade" (a chain of prior-family lookups), not kernel/cascade.js (BFS reachability over a dependency graph) -- confirmed by reading prior-query.js directly; kernel/cascade.js itself has zero references in either registry, genuinely unowned.

The dependency relation: two claims are connected when they share a role filler (the same ARG0 or ARG1 value) -- a mechanical proxy for shared-entity/coreference connection, consistent with how this project already treats shared referents elsewhere (finish.js's takesUp, referents.js's resolved beings), not a newly invented notion. claimDependencyIndex(claims) builds kernel/cascade.js's own dependentsIndex from this relation; seedsOfClaimFiller(slot, value) seeds only from role-shaped slots (matching fold-at.js's own slotsFromClaims naming), never from rel or polarity, which carry no shareable entity. 4 tests pass, including one against real claims from gpgp.md confirming real role fillers are genuinely shared across more than one real claim, not just true on synthetic data. Full existing suite re-verified: 25 tests across fold-at, claims-from-feat and cli/fold-at, no regressions.

Built and tested standalone only -- NOT yet wired into fold-at.js's significance field or the CLI, which remains the next concrete step: call consequentialSurprise(holo, facts, {index, seedsOf: seedsOfClaimFiller, ...}) inside foldAt when the caller supplies an index (built via claimDependencyIndex), alongside the existing predict()-only path, and measure whether it produces a genuinely different (and genuinely load-bearing) partition on real material -- not attempted this revision. Re-tested Ollama: still down.

REVISION, 2026-09-26 (scheduled cron firing, completing the wiring named as the concrete next step last cycle): fold-at.js's significance field now carries a real significance.consequential sub-field, wired to kernel/consequential-surprise.js via last cycle's claim-dependencies.js (claimDependencyIndex, seedsOfClaimFiller). One real conflict had to be resolved first: consequentialSurprise(holo, facts, ...) calls admit() INTERNALLY (confirmed by reading its source), which mutates the holograph -- unlike predict(), the only thing the existing significance path used, specifically to preserve foldAt's own tested purity guarantee. Resolved with a real cloneHolograph(holo) helper (deep-copying every field admit()/createHolograph() actually touch: schema, alpha, gamma, admitted, slots, absentMass, verified by reading both this revision) and running consequentialSurprise only on the clone. pValue is never defaulted (consequentialSurprise's own guard throws without one, and this project's standing rule already forbids hand-set thresholds) -- the layer activates only when the caller supplies holo, index, seedsOf, AND pValue together; any one missing stays an honest gap.

Verified end to end with a real ad hoc script before writing tests: three synthetic claims sharing "author" and "ocean" fillers produced real loadBearing:true rows, and the caller's original holograph's .admitted stayed at 0 throughout. 4 new committed tests lock this in (the gap case, the wired case with real rows, and two separate mutation checks -- one for the existing predict() path, one for the new consequential path), using the test file's own existing fixture claims (which already share "the-general"/"the-order" across two grounds) rather than new synthetic data. Full related suite re-verified: 33 tests across fold-at, claim-dependencies, claims-from-feat (both), and cli/fold-at -- no regressions.

Not yet done, named as the next step: the CLI (cli/fold-at.mjs) does not yet pass index/seedsOf/pValue, so its own printed output still shows the consequential gap even though the library now supports it -- wiring the CLI, and choosing/disclosing a real pValue rather than an arbitrary one, is the natural next increment. Re-tested Ollama: still down.

title: How this vision gets chased, not just stated (revised: cli/fold-at.mjs exposes consequential-surprise via a required, never-defaulted --pvalue)
text:
